d:
As a Watcher, I was allowed access to many of Medivh's personal effects. Among those items, I found the tomes most enlightening. While the majority of the books were filled with - to put it bluntly - tripe, there were some gems. One of those tomes documented the creation of a set of armor fit for an archmage: Frostfire.
It's all in here and I am willing to share the fruits of that knowledge with you as long as you are able to provide me with the necessary materials.
human-female
p: You got some missing parts for the quest please go and get them all!
c:
Exellent friend!,
You got everything just as i asked and now i can make a Frostfire Gloves.

Father Montoy makes some strange gestures in the air in front of you.
Blessed kid, have you found the vestments of the fallen? The poor souls whose last breaths were taken on the field of battle - stripped of everything including their dignity.
Bring me the desecrated remnants of the departed along with reagents of purification and you shall know faith.
human-male
p: Have you brought me the reagents, child?
c: The vestments are ready, friend. Smite those that would harm our world in your righteous fire.

d:
The phylactery is all that remains of the master of Naxxramas. Your better judgment dictates that you destroy the phylactery, preventing the lich from ever reforming. Thankfully, you seldom listen to that internal voice of reason.
Someone at Light's Hope will pay you hugely for this artifact. Who cares if Kel'Thuzad regenerates to full power?

In the thick of Plaguewood lies the entrance to the dread citadel of Naxxramas. Previously, all attempts to enter had been stymied by the magical wards placed upon the rune portal. That is, until now.
We have devised a way to gain entry via arcane cloaking - an old cantrip of the Kirin Tor with a few modifications of my own. Since your dedication to the cause of the Dawn is somewhat lacking, friend, the price will be high. You may decline and choose to return when you are revered or exalted for a discount.
human-female
p: None have entered Naxxramas and lived to tell the tale.
c: You will feel a slight tingle, friend. That sensation means it's working. Once complete, you will be able to enter Naxxramas by stepping upon the rune portal in Plaguewood.

d:
In the thick of Plaguewood lies the entrance to the dread citadel of Naxxramas. Previously, all attempts to enter had been stymied by the magical wards placed upon the rune portal. That is, until now.
We have devised a way to gain entry via a permanent arcane cloaking of sorts - an old cantrip of the Kirin Tor with a few modifications of my own. With that said, the cloaking is costly. Since your dedication to the cause of the Dawn is admirable, we are willing to incur some of those costs.
human-female

c: You will feel a slight tingle, friend. That sensation means it's working. Once complete, you will be able to enter Naxxramas by stepping upon the rune portal in Plaguewood.

We have devised a way to gain entry via a permanent arcane cloaking of sorts - an old cantrip of the Kirin Tor with a few modifications of my own. With that said, the cloaking is costly; however, your dedication to the cause of the Dawn is unwavering! We will waive all cost associations.
human-female

c: You will feel a slight tingle, friend. That sensation means it's working. Once complete, you will be able to enter Naxxramas by stepping upon the rune portal in Plaguewood.

d:
How would you like to earn yourself one of these shiny coins?
I've got a little problem that you might be able to help me with, friend. You see, I make Cryptstalker armor for those daft enough to venture into Naxxramas. While they supply me with the core material requirements for the armor, I always run out of the crypt fiend parts. Bring me back a bundle of parts and I'll pay you with an insignia - usable at the quartermaster.
human-male
c: Ah, that'll do nicely, friend. Remember, I'm always accepting more parts. For every bundle you bring me, I'll reward you with an insignia.

p: You did an exemplary job on the first bundle, friend. If you have more, I will take them now. For every bundle that you turn in, I will reward you with another insignia.
c: Most excellent, friend! These will definitely come to good use.

d:
Don Julio's Bonescythe armor pattern requires bone fragments - a lot of bone fragments. While those crazy enough to venture into Naxxramas provide me with enough of the core materials to make the armor, I'm always looking for more Scourge bone fragments.
So what do you think? Interested in getting your hands dirty and destroying some Scourge at the same time? It's a win-win situation.
human-male
p: I can direct you to skeleton infested locales, adventurer.
c:
You work fast, friend. Fast like a fox... Say, have I ever told you about the time I was in a barber shop quartet?
Remind me to tell you that story one of these days.

p: A man in my line of work can never have too many bone fragments, friend. Whenever you have a surplus of fragments, bring them to me and I'll reward you with another insignia.
c: My dream of becoming a full-time dancer at the Gadgetzan disco is soon to become a reality! Keep up the good work, friend.

d:
Greetings, adventurer! Are you interested in some work? I pay those under my employ with insignias. These insignias can be used at the Quartermaster to purchase items of power.
All I need you to do is bring me as many core of elements as you can carry. The more the better!
You'll find them on elementals of varying shapes and sizes that exist across our world.
human-female
p: I can only steer you in the right direction, friend.
c: A job well done, friend! As promised, the insignia is yours. Just remember, there's more where that came from...

p:
Truth be told, I use the cores to create Frostfire armor. It is the armor used by the mages battling in Naxxramas. Without you and others like you, we would most definitely be losing this war.
With that said, bring me more cores and I shall grant you more insignias.
c: You perform a great service for us, friend. Well done!

d:
Have you ever seen Dreadnaught armor, adventurer? No, of course you haven't. You're still a kid - a tyke. Let me tell you, it is glorious.
You're probably asking yourself what any of this has to do with you, right? I'll tell you what, scrub; I need Dark Iron scraps and I'm willing to pay to get my hands on as many as possible.
I need the scraps to put together sets of Dreadnaught for our champions. Bring me scraps and get paid.
human-male
p: What do you want? Directions? I can provide those...
c: This will do, for now. If you get more, you know where to find me.

p: For every armful of the scraps, I'll give you an insignia - the more the better. Now get out of my sight before I split you in two!
c: That's all you brought me? Maybe you didn't hear me the first time. I need MORE!

d:
I make a special type of armor for the brave heroes that enter Naxxramas known as Dreamwalker. They are able to provide me with most of the materials I require but I am always looking for those able to retrieve savage fronds from the flora of our world.
You may think of this job as beneath you, but without the fronds, the armor could not be made.
I am also in a unique position to pay you with an insignia of your choice as both the Dawn and the Crusade supply me with funds.
nightelf-female
p: I have intimate knowledge of the flora in our world. Do you require direction?
c:
I am much obliged, friend.
Please remember that I am always accepting fronds.

p:
For every bundle of fronds that you deliver to me, I will pay you with your choice of an insignia of the Dawn or the Crusade.
Insignias may be turned in to the Quartermaster for various rewards.
c: Thank you, friend. Your work is vital to the success of our campaign against the Scourge.

d:
You want a writ? What? Do you expect me to hand you a highly sought after work order just for showing up? I think not, scrub. Crafters from around the world bid for jobs here at the front lines.
If you want a work order, you'll have to show me that you're willing to bleed for the cause. Bring me a valor token and we'll talk.
And there's only one way to get your grubby little scrub mitts on those - get to killin'.
human-male
p: What is it? I'm a busy man.
c: Alright, here's how it works: For every valor token that you turn in, I'll give you another writ. You complete the order on that writ and deliver the order to Packmaster Stonebruiser. Got it? Good. Now get out of here.

p: You know the drill, kid. One valor token gets you a craftsman's writ.
c: You earned this, scrub. Now, don't cry about your orders. Fill 'em or destroy 'em.

d:
The floating necropolises of the Scourge plague the lands of Horde and Alliance alike. Tanaris, the Blasted Lands, Winterspring and the Burning Steppes are blanketed in the shadows of the flying fortresses.
Only through our combined efforts will they be turned away.
The necropolises are supported by magical circles at various points in the invaded areas. We have determined that destroying the mindless hordes that surround these circles will destroy their defenses.
human-male
p: It will take time to prevail against this threat. How have you fared, friend?
c:
You've done well, friend. Through these incremental defeats, we shall prevail against this renewed Scourge threat.
Rest and recover, but then you must head out to the front again, lest we lose the ground we have gained today.
To aid you in your further battles, we will make some of our special items available to you in trade for more necrotic runes.

d:
The Scourge have returned in greater numbers than we have seen before. The Argent Dawn is recruiting all willing and capable men and women to defend our lands.
If we share common cause, take this document to the Keeper of the Rolls at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands.
human-male
p: You've come to join our order, have you not?
c: The Argent Dawn placed the call for aid, and you, among others, have answered. There is no time for us to provide you with training. Our faith is placed in your abilities, and that you will join us in throwing back this Scourge threat.

d:
Without the help of adventurers, my caravan would have never made it! Scourge were coming out of the woodwork to try and stop us from getting here.
Now we need to wait here for Field Marshal Chambers to arrive. He'll sign your writ of safe passage to take back to Dispatch Commander Metz at Light's Hope Chapel.
And friend, watch what you say around Chambers. He's the 'bite off your head and spit down your wind pipe' type of guy - except that he'll actually do it...
dwarf-male
c: Excellent work, friend. Outstanding even! Take this as a token of our appreciation. No pun intended, scrub.

d:

120 Dense Weightstones.
All filled orders should be delivered to Packmaster Stonebruiser at Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands.
Contract is null and void if tampered with or damaged.
-Dispatch Commander Metz, The Argent Dawn
c: Yep, these will come in handy for the infantry's bashin' weapons.

Blessed bootstraps! Are those what I think they are? The troops have been complaining non-stop about the lack of storage space for all that is required while in the field. One of them even drew me a diagram - such a pansy...
These will definitely help alleviate some of the whining.

d:

c:
You shouldn't have! No really, you shouldn't have. I don't know what Metz is thinking, but nobody is going to be wearing these robes into Naxxramas.
Bah, another pile of junk I'll have to get transferred to the front lines and another berating I'll have to take from Chambers.
